steps.title: Find the homes
steps.why: First find where this repo keeps rules and tests. That way you add files beside the code that owns them.
steps.deliverable: Write down the game package, test folder, frontend app, service route, storage module, and run commands.
steps.placement: Use the paths that already exist in your teammate's repo. If it looks like this repo, inspect packages/, services/, and frontend/ first.
steps.pattern: Keep each rule, route, test, and data file near its current owner.
steps.check: You can name the test command and folder where a Match rule test should go.

steps.title: Make a small Match core
steps.why: Submit needs a Match, an active Round, a player, a phase, and a clock.
steps.deliverable: Create Match and Round state, legal phase changes, score rules, a fixed clock, and a fake Judge test helper.
steps.placement: Use the existing game-rules package. In a similar layout, create packages/arena-game/src/match-rules.ts and packages/arena-game/test/match-rules.test.ts.
steps.pattern: Keep phase and score choices in a pure rule module. Pass in the clock and fake Judge result in tests.
steps.check: A fixed-clock test starts a Match and Round, then rejects an action in the wrong phase.

steps.title: Give a player a Problem and Run
steps.why: A player and visible Problem must exist before code can be checked or submitted.
steps.deliverable: Add basic Match entry, one checked Problem, and a Run that returns example feedback without changing the score.
steps.placement: In a similar layout, put Match entry near packages/arena-game/src/lobby.ts and its test near packages/arena-game/test/lobby.test.ts. Put Problem data under packages/problem-bank/problems/.
steps.pattern: Keep Problem data separate from Match rules. Run returns visible feedback and does not change the score.
steps.check: An admitted player can Run visible examples. A visitor is rejected, and no Run changes the score.

steps.title: Add Submission and Reveal
steps.why: Now the game can decide when code may enter hidden tests and when its score can be shown.
steps.deliverable: Add Submit, a pending receipt, retry identity, a fake-Judge result, the deadline cutoff, score update, and Reveal.
steps.placement: In a similar layout, extend packages/arena-game/src/engine.ts and add a test in packages/arena-game/test/submit-path.test.ts. Use the Judge interface your repo already has.
steps.pattern: Game rules decide if Submit is legal, storage records acceptance, and the Judge runs code. Use the same request ID for a retry.
steps.check: A valid Submit is judged once. Submit after Round close is rejected. Hidden results appear only at Reveal.

steps.title: Save accepted Match state
steps.why: Reconnect and restart need to recover saved Submissions and Reveals.
steps.deliverable: Add one Match storage contract, an in-memory version, then a database adapter and restart tests.
steps.placement: In a similar layout, extend packages/arena-game/src/persistence.ts and packages/arena-game/test/persistence.test.ts, then use the existing database adapter.
steps.pattern: Test one storage contract with memory and the real database. Reject writes based on an old revision.
steps.check: After restart, the same accepted Submission and Reveal are loaded. An old write cannot replace newer state.

steps.title: Connect players to the rules
steps.why: The screen should send commands and show the Match state owned by the server.
steps.deliverable: Add a service route, transport, basic Arena screen, and reconnect snapshot behavior.
steps.placement: In a similar layout, find the game service under services/game/src/game/, transport under frontend/src/arena/transport.ts, and screen under frontend/src/components/. Test each at its boundary.
steps.pattern: The screen sends commands and shows server state. Transport handles delivery and reconnect.
steps.check: Two browser clients see the same saved Match. After reconnect, the client loads its current state.

steps.title: Add two-player teams
steps.why: Shared editing and Ready checks need Match rules, storage, and live messages first.
steps.deliverable: Add 2v2 teams, a shared revision, Readiness reset after edits, team-only chat, and reconnect tests.
steps.placement: In a similar layout, extend packages/arena-game/src/team-collaboration.ts and its test. Keep clients in frontend/src/arena/collab.ts and chat.ts.
steps.pattern: Game rules own Readiness and revision. Collaboration and chat clients deliver team-scoped updates.
steps.check: Four users stay separated by team. An edit clears both Readiness approvals.

steps.title: Check the real boundaries
steps.why: Fake tests do not prove PostgreSQL, Docker isolation, or real browser behavior.
steps.deliverable: Run equivalent database, Judge security, and two-client browser checks in your teammate's repo. Record checks that could not run separately.
steps.placement: Use the existing database, Judge, and browser test folders. In a similar layout, inspect packages/arena-game/test/judge-security.test.ts and frontend/e2e/.
steps.pattern: Keep fake, database, Docker, and real-browser evidence separate. Record the command and result for each.
steps.check: Mark PASS only after the matching test runs in your teammate's repo and passes.
